title: Manipulating and Changing Styles of HTML Elements with Javascript
summary: Shows how to change an element's CSS from JavaScript through its style property: CSS names become camelCase and all values are strings. Ends with a challenge to turn a button's background yellow.

concepts.heading: The style property
points: Every selected element has a style object; assign to its properties to set inline styles, e.g. document.querySelector('h1').style.color = 'red'.
Any CSS property can be set this way.

concepts.heading: Name conversion rule
points: JavaScript names for properties and methods use camelCase (first word lowercase, later words capitalised), like querySelector.
So hyphenated CSS names lose the dash and capitalise the next word: font-size becomes fontSize, background-color becomes backgroundColor. Single-word properties (color, padding) stay the same.
The DOM style object reference on MDN lists every property name; searching it for the CSS name finds the JS spelling.

concepts.heading: Values are always strings
points: In CSS the value is typed bare (padding: 7%); in JS the value must be a quoted string even if numeric-looking, e.g. style.padding = '7%' or style.fontSize = '10rem'.
Same for keywords: visibility hidden becomes style.visibility = 'hidden'. The Elements panel in DevTools can be used to preview a CSS edit before writing the JS.

concepts.heading: Challenge solution
points: CSS equivalent: background-color: yellow, so the JS property is backgroundColor.
Select the button with querySelector('button') (or '.btn') and assign the string 'yellow'.

concepts.heading: Next step
points: The following lesson covers separation of concerns: keeping styling in CSS and using JavaScript only to switch it on or off.

task.goal: Change the button's background colour from the console using JS.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 16 - The Document Object Model (DOM)/16.04 - Manipulating and Changing Styles of HTML Elements with Javascript/script.js

pitfalls: Writing style.background-color (a syntax error: JS reads the dash as subtraction); use backgroundColor.
Forgetting units: style.fontSize = 10 is ignored; use '10rem'.
(Extra) Inline styles override stylesheet rules, so they can be hard to undo; that is why the next lesson moves styling back into CSS classes.
Reference repo diverges: its script is run on load rather than from the console and the page has a student footer (omitted).
